primitives.name: Flexible Intersection Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our contributions are 1) flexible intersection selection and 2) intersection refinement to improve accuracy in calibration.
primitives.assumptions: Field lines are detectable and their intersections form a structured grid; intersections are not solely constrained to horizontal/vertical line combinations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When field line detection fails or when intersections are ambiguous due to occlusion or low contrast.

layer2.mapping: Maps detected line intersections to a canonical field template space via point matching; enables robust spatial correspondence estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Intersection count and geometric consistency score between detected and expected field layout.

primitives.name: Intersection Refinement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Our proposed method can solve these problems by flexible intersection selection and refinement.
primitives.assumptions: Detected intersections deviate from true positions due to noise or misalignment; local field line re-detection improves accuracy.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When initial intersection estimates are inaccurate due to sensor or environmental distortion.

layer2.mapping: Iteratively adjusts intersection coordinates based on neighboring line segments; reduces displacement error in image-space coordinates.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared deviation of refined intersections from ground truth or prior estimates.

primitives.name: Homography Matrix Estimation
primitives.verbatim_quote: A homography matrix is used to convert world coordinates to image coordinates for the calibration.
primitives.assumptions: Planar field surface exists; known correspondences between world and image points exist.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When field is non-planar or when insufficient point correspondences are available for stable estimation.

layer2.mapping: Establishes projective transformation between 2D image plane and 2D world plane; enables back-projection of player positions.
layer2.telemetry: Reprojection error of matched points after applying estimated homography.

The core innovation lies in improving camera calibration accuracy for sports scenes by addressing two key limitations of conventional approaches: fixed intersection selection and lack of refinement. The flexible intersection selection allows for more robust identification of intersections beyond simple horizontal-vertical grids, enhancing generalization across different sports fields. Intersection refinement mitigates positional errors caused by detection inaccuracies or environmental distortions. These primitives are composed into a pipeline where field lines are first detected, then intersections are computed and refined before generating point matches against a known field template. From these matches, a homography matrix is estimated that maps image coordinates to world coordinates. This process enables precise tracking of players' movements in real-world space from video input. Failure modes include poor line detection under low-light conditions or misalignment of the field template, leading to incorrect point correspondences and thus inaccurate homography estimation.
